High plasma osmotic concentration supports ADH release, greater kidney water reabsorption, and more concentrated urine.
Saying aldosterone and ADH are the same hormone because both can affect body water.
words.definition: Coordinated neural, endocrine, and kidney responses that regulate water balance, sodium handling, osmotic concentration, and blood volume or pressure.

structure.text: ADH: antidiuretic hormone. anti-: against. diuresis: urine production. osmo-: osmotic movement or concentration. ADH reduces water loss; it does not mean that urine production stops completely.
structure.caution: ADH reduces water loss; it does not mean that urine production stops completely.

words.whatItDoes: Osmoreceptors influence ADH release and kidney water reabsorption; aldosterone changes sodium reabsorption, with water effects depending on gradients and other controls.
words.commonConfusion: Plasma osmotic concentration and blood volume provide related but different evidence and should not be treated as one identical variable.
words.retrievalPrompt: Explain the evidence pattern expected when plasma osmotic concentration is high but ADH action is insufficient.

words.definition: Antidiuretic hormone, also called vasopressin, which regulates water conservation among other effects.

structure.text: Initialism for antidiuretic hormone; anti- opposes diuresis, urine-water loss.

words.whatItDoes: It increases water permeability in kidney collecting pathways under relevant conditions.
words.commonConfusion: It is synthesized in the hypothalamus, not in the posterior pituitary that releases it.
words.retrievalPrompt: How does greater kidney water reabsorption affect urine concentration?

words.definition: An adrenal-cortex hormone important in sodium and potassium balance.

structure.text: Aldosterone is a whole steroid-hormone name; it is distinct from ADH.

words.whatItDoes: It promotes renal sodium reabsorption and potassium secretion, influencing fluid balance.
words.commonConfusion: Sodium retention and direct water-channel regulation are not the same mechanism.
words.retrievalPrompt: How do aldosterone and ADH differ in their kidney effects?

words.definition: A receptor responsive to changes in osmotic conditions.

structure.text: Osmo- refers to osmotic conditions; receptor identifies detection.

words.whatItDoes: Changes in cell water balance contribute to signals controlling thirst and ADH.
words.commonConfusion: It does not directly count every solute molecule consciously.
words.retrievalPrompt: Why can increased extracellular concentration stimulate water-conserving responses?

words.definition: The concentration of osmotically active particles in a solution.

structure.text: Osmotic qualifies concentration by particle effects on water movement.

words.whatItDoes: Differences across a selectively permeable membrane influence water movement.
words.commonConfusion: Mass concentration alone may not represent the number of dissolved particles.
words.retrievalPrompt: Why do particle number and membrane permeability matter?

modelFrayer: Neural and endocrine adjustments that help the body respond to challenge and recover afterward.
Includes a fast sympathetic-adrenal-medulla route and a slower ACTH-cortisol route with distinct timing.
A sudden alarm rapidly increases sympathetic output and epinephrine while longer challenge can sustain cortisol effects.
Treating cortisol and epinephrine as interchangeable names for one identical signal.
words.definition: Coordinated neural and endocrine responses that adjust energy use, circulation, and other functions during challenge and support return toward a workable range afterward.

structure.text: ACTH: adrenocorticotropic hormone. adrenal: near the kidney. cortex: outer layer. medulla: inner region. Acronym and anatomical clues identify pathway parts but do not make every stress response identical.
structure.caution: Acronym and anatomical clues identify pathway parts but do not make every stress response identical.

words.whatItDoes: Fast autonomic signalling activates adrenal-medulla epinephrine release; a slower hypothalamus-pituitary-adrenal pathway supports adrenal-cortex cortisol release.
words.commonConfusion: Cortisol and epinephrine differ in source, timing, receptor pathways, and effects; stress is not one hormone or always harmful.
words.retrievalPrompt: Contrast the fast adrenal-medulla pathway with the slower ACTH-cortisol pathway.

words.definition: Adrenocorticotropic hormone, an anterior-pituitary signal regulating adrenal-cortex activity.

structure.text: Initialism for adrenocorticotropic hormone: adreno- adrenal, cortico- cortex, tropic endocrine stimulation.

words.whatItDoes: It stimulates cortisol secretion within the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis.
words.commonConfusion: It does not directly name an adrenal-medulla catecholamine.
words.retrievalPrompt: What feedback would increased cortisol exert in an intact axis?

words.definition: An adrenal-cortex glucocorticoid hormone affecting metabolism and stress responses.

structure.text: Cortisol is a whole hormone name; glucocorticoid identifies a steroid class, not glucose itself.

words.whatItDoes: It changes substrate availability and influences many tissues through receptor-mediated regulation.
words.commonConfusion: Cortisol is not identical to the rapid neural alarm response.
words.retrievalPrompt: Why can cortisol responses have different timing from epinephrine responses?

words.definition: A catecholamine hormone from the adrenal medulla, also called adrenaline.

structure.text: Epinephrine and adrenaline are alternate names for the same molecule.

words.whatItDoes: Adrenergic receptors mediate effects supporting acute adjustments in circulation and metabolism.
words.commonConfusion: It is not made by the adrenal cortex.
words.retrievalPrompt: Why does its action differ among receptor-bearing organs?

words.definition: The outer region of the adrenal gland that produces steroid hormones.

structure.text: Adrenal identifies the gland; cortex means its outer region.

words.whatItDoes: Its zones produce hormone classes including glucocorticoids and mineralocorticoids.
words.commonConfusion: It is distinct from the catecholamine-producing medulla.
words.retrievalPrompt: Which adrenal region produces cortisol and aldosterone?

words.definition: The inner region of the adrenal gland containing catecholamine-secreting cells.

structure.text: Medulla identifies an inner region; adrenal distinguishes it from other organs' medullae.

words.whatItDoes: Sympathetic input can trigger epinephrine and norepinephrine release.
words.commonConfusion: It does not produce the same steroid hormones as the cortex.
words.retrievalPrompt: How does its neural input connect nervous and endocrine responses?
